after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={90}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{90}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{90}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{90}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (0)+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={60}^{∘}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+{60}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={60}^{∘}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+{60}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
